hypotheses.reasoning: The trigger is session-cache restarting at 22:04:17 after a node replacement with no RDB snapshot, so it came back with 0 keys (#2828). Within 30s account-svc's session-cache miss ratio jumped from a 6% baseline to 93%, and every login fell through to accounts-db (#2887). That cold-cache load drove accounts-db to 98-100% CPU and 490/500 connections (#2921), and it ran sequential scans on audit_log (#2897). Account queries then timed out after 5s (#3045), and edge-proxy returned POST /login 504s (#3049). The 504s at the edge, the notification 503s and the template circuit breaker are downstream spread, not origins. Alternative: config_error (no persistence/snapshot configured on session-cache) could be the underlying gap; resource_exhaustion of the DB pool fits the symptoms, but onset tracks the cache restart and the DB saturated only after the miss storm.

Session-cache restarted with no RDB snapshot available, which suggests a persistence/snapshot misconfiguration after node replacement. That makes the empty cache possible, but the outage itself is the miss stampede onto accounts-db.
accounts-db ran out of connection slots and CPU. This is the saturated resource, but it was driven by the cache-miss load rather than starting on its own.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore session-cache from the last good snapshot or pre-warm it, and enable RDB persistence so a node replacement does not start cold. Short term, throttle or single-flight the account-svc cache-miss path to accounts-db, and add an index for the audit_log seq scan. Once accounts-db CPU and connections recover, confirm login 504s drop. The metrics-agent queue drops and the template-svc mailer circuit breaker are unrelated to this incident.

Within 30s account-svc's session-cache miss ratio jumped from a 6% baseline to 93%, and every login fell through to accounts-db (#2887).
